title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f67v2 Sun/Moon titles may name the opposite path endpoint
summary: An old ledger-only audit reports ol in two Moon-endpoint titles but H/Hd in two Sun-endpoint titles on f67v2, while its previously consumed other solar/lunar panels reportedly make ol point SUN or fail and H point MOON or fail. A source-endpoint rather than destination-endpoint interpretation could reconcile that reversal under one fixed rule. This is a hypothesis from an imported historical summary, not a re-audit: the cited primary report is unavailable at its recorded path, f67v2 is not in the current admitted image/text lists, the old external panels are not fresh confirmation, and neither path direction nor title ownership is independently fixed. No target content, sealed data or reserve is opened. Do not infer ol=SUN, H=MOON or any lexeme from the present pattern.

design.mechanism: A path title names its source body, whereas the earlier endpoint inventory associated it with its drawn destination.
design.unit: All four historically documented f67v2 E1 path titles and every independently owned solar/lunar title comparator, only after current access and the missing primary are resolved.
design.contrast: One fixed source-body relation versus destination-body relation or nonreferential path/class descriptions.
design.prediction: If a source direction can be fixed without the candidate words, the source model predicts that the two Moon-endpoint titles refer to Sun sources and the two Sun-endpoint titles to Moon sources, with the reverse for the destination model. The exact whole titles and all external comparators must keep one assignment; one contradictory owned path or absent direction rejects selection.
